newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Spain cuts key rate to 5.50 pct.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Spain cuts key rate to 5.50 pct.

text.p: Following are analysts' comments on the Bank of Spain's decision to lower its key money market rate to 5.50 percent from 5.75 percent at its regular repurchase auction on Tuesday.
In a Reuter survey of 11 analysts and dealers conducted on Monday, 10 had expected a reduction given the recent downtrend in inflation and the peseta's relative strength.
VALENTIN FERNANDEZ, ECONOMIST AT CREDIT LYONNAIS IN MADRID
"Prices were discounting such a decision. It would have been strange if it had done anything else. The peseta was strong.
"Further moves will depend on the domestic inflation trend and the euro mood. If these two things go in the right direction we'll have more cuts, small ones, during the year.

"This time we had a classic case of buying on the rumour and selling on the fact. We have profit-taking especially in the short end and to see our market gaining more we need more quiet in foreign markets."
GREGORIO GOMEZ, MADRID-BASED ECONOMIST
"The cut was discounted, and given the favourable macroeconomic scenario more than justified.
"In the sense that the the cut was discounted by the markets it could prompt some short-term profit-taking.
"I expect our markets this week to trade sideways or consolidate, but in a while the upward tone will resume given continued expectations of new cuts."
ALFREDO URRUTIA, ECONOMIST AT SOCIETE GENERALE IN MADRID-RFTV
"The move has been cautious...the Bank of Spain can cut once more with another CPI number before U.S. Federal Reserve FOMC. So the move has been cautious.

(The Bank of Spain) has the room for additional cuts during the year. If we could be sure that Spain will be in EMU from day one that would give additional room for bullishness. We agreed that five percent could be the limit (this year).
The Bank of Spain will try to cut ahead (of possible Fed tightening)... and if the Fed hikes rates on May 20 the Bank of Spain still would have 25 basis points that it would take a while to use.
Inflation could pick up in the second part of the year, but still it will remain at a very good level for Spain."
MARCO PIANELLI, ECONOMIST AT NOMURA IN LONDON-RFTV
"The Bank of Spain surely thinks that the rate can be cut further this year. We are looking for the rate to be around 5 percent by the end of this year.
It's much easier in Spain to cut rates (than in Italy), they do not have as much debt to finance as Italy has and the political enviroment is different.
Given what they have done this month and given what will likely be a good CPI, the market will anticipate another cuts. The Bank of Spain, however, will be very cautious.
Spain's inflation is still going down....We expect it to go
ANTONIO GARCIA REBOLLAR, DIRECTOR RENTA 4 - MADRID

"This rate cut was necessary, expected and coherent with the recent behaviour of markets. I expect new and important rate cuts with a view to the development of CPI, although they will be linked to market stability, fundamentally with the exchange rate of the peseta and with long-term 10-year interest rates, which is very important for the Bank of Spain. They will also be tied to the development of the public deficit."
--Madrid Newsroom +34 1 585 2167
